item.title: SEE IT: Chinese nationals intercepted in ‘extremely dangerous’ infiltration attempt near Florida coast
item.description: Video shows CBP and the Coast Guard intercepting a 27-foot vessel near Key Largo carrying 13 Chinese nationals and other illegal immigrants.
item.content:encoded:
A smuggling vessel filled with Chinese nationals and other illegal immigrants was intercepted by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and the Coast Guard in what sources called a rare and "extremely dangerous" attempt to enter the U.S. through Florida.

CBP confirmed the interdiction exclusively with Fox News, sharing video and photos of U.S. authorities intercepting the vessel, which was carrying 22 illegal immigrants, including 13 Chinese nationals. The boat, a 27-foot cuddy cabin vessel, was stopped, and the migrants aboard were arrested without incident Tuesday. The interdiction took place near Angelfish Creek, Florida, near Key Largo.

According to the agency, a CBP Air and Marine Operations multi-role enforcement aircraft first detected the vessel. The interdiction, carried out by CBP alongside Coast Guard personnel, resulted in the apprehension of one suspected smuggler, a Cuban national, 13 Chinese nationals, eight Ecuadorian nationals and one Dominican national.

Sources emphasized to Fox News that it is extremely rare for Chinese nationals to attempt to enter the U.S. through maritime Caribbean routes that are typically used by Haitians, Dominicans and Cubans. During the Biden administration, Chinese nationals typically entered the U.S. through land routes in California and Texas, which are now subject to tighter enforcement under the Trump administration.

CBP, COAST GUARD INTERCEPT MIGRANT VESSEL HEADING FOR PUERTO RICO; 40 APPREHENDED INCLUDING UZBEK NATIONAL

Andres Blanco, executive director of Air and Marine Operations Southeast Region, told Fox News that "attempting to enter the United States illegally by sea is extremely dangerous and will not go undetected."

Blanco said that "this interdiction demonstrates the strength of our maritime partnerships and our commitment to stopping human smuggling organizations before they can put more lives at risk."

He added that "those who attempt these dangerous voyages face arrest, prosecution, removal, and the very real possibility of losing their lives at sea."

The illegal immigrants were transferred to the U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Pablo Valent for processing. Meanwhile, authorities seized the vessel.

ICE-LED FLORIDA OPERATION NETS 500 — INCLUDING ILLEGAL ALIENS ACCUSED OF MURDER, CHILD ABUSE, CARTEL TIES

After the operation, Coast Guard Lt. Corryn Ulrich, the commanding officer of the Pablo Valent, told Fox News that "the U.S. border remains secure due to highly capable teams and coordinated interagency enforcement" and that "we remain ready to save lives and enforce federal law at sea."

The CBP Air and Marine Operations unit is designed to anticipate and confront aviation and maritime threats to America’s national integrity, according to the agency.

President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to meet Thursday in Washington, D.C.

Gatestone Institute senior fellow Gordon Chang claimed that, despite the leaders trumpeting a positive relationship, Xi is mulling a war against the United States and organizing troops "for battle."

"Xi Jinping keeps on talking about going to war against us… and also he's preparing China's society, civilian and military, for battle. And we think we're at peace," Chang said Sunday on "Fox News Live." "So, this is a very dangerous period for us."

Chang’s remarks follow reports that China aided Iran in attacks that killed three U.S. troops in Jordan earlier this summer.

ICE SHOOTING ROCKS AUSTIN AS DEMOCRAT DEMANDS BODYCAM VIDEO, INDEPENDENT PROBE

The incident comes amid renewed debate over the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement tactics after a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer shot a Venezuelan illegal immigrant in Austin on Sunday. The Department of Homeland Security said the man shot by the officer, Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, "illegally entered the country under the Biden administration and had a final order of removal during a law enforcement operation."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

His lawyer, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, has contested DHS’ statement, saying Perez entered the U.S. lawfully. According to DHS, he survived and is in stable condition and is in federal custody pending removal. The incident has resulted in large protests in Austin and Democratic politicians condemning ICE and the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement.

Fox News Digital's Nora Moriarty and Stepheny Price contributed to this report.

item.title: 3 VPN settings to check before your next trip
item.description: Your VPN may quietly drop protection when switching between airport Wi-Fi and hotel Wi-Fi. Key settings like auto-connect and kill switch help.
item.content:encoded:
Has this happened to you? You're at the airport, connected to the terminal Wi-Fi, VPN running and feeling good about your security. You board, put your phone in airplane mode, land a few hours later and switch airplane mode off. Your phone finds the hotel Wi-Fi. You open your email and start scrolling.

What you probably didn't notice is the moment in between. For a few seconds, your phone may have been reconnecting while your VPN was still catching up. During that brief window, some traffic could have left your device without VPN protection.

Most websites today use HTTPS encryption, so losing your VPN for a few seconds does not mean everything you do suddenly becomes visible. Still, a VPN adds another layer of privacy, particularly when you are connecting to airport, hotel and coffee shop networks you do not control. Here's how you can reduce those connection gaps while traveling.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

HOW TO STREAM SAFELY WHILE TRAVELING OUTSIDE THE US

A VPN works by building an encrypted tunnel between your device and the internet. While that tunnel is active, your connection to the VPN server is encrypted. However, the VPN relies on an internet connection. When your phone drops one network and connects to another, the VPN may need to re-establish that tunnel.

Usually, this happens so quickly that you barely notice. However, a weak signal, slow hotel login page or network that takes a few extra seconds to connect can create a brief period when your device has internet access before the VPN reconnects.

This can happen during completely ordinary activities. You might switch from cellular data to airport Wi-Fi after landing. Later, your phone may move from the airport network to your hotel's Wi-Fi. The same thing can happen when your phone wakes from sleep in a new location or reconnects after losing cellular service. For travelers who move between networks frequently, those transitions are worth paying attention to.

When your VPN is disconnected, websites and online services can generally see the public IP address assigned by your internet provider or Wi-Fi network instead of the VPN server's IP address. That address can reveal information such as your approximate location and internet provider.

A VPN also helps prevent the operator of a Wi-Fi network from easily seeing details about the internet services your device is contacting. Most trusted websites and apps already encrypt sensitive traffic using HTTPS or other encryption. That greatly reduces what someone monitoring a public Wi-Fi connection can see.

However, risks remain if you connect to a fake or compromised Wi-Fi network. Someone controlling the network may try to direct you to a fraudulent login page, interfere with your connection or exploit websites and apps that are not properly encrypted.

A VPN adds another layer of protection by encrypting traffic between your device and the VPN server and masking your normal public IP address. A kill switch can provide an additional safeguard by preventing internet traffic from leaving your device if the VPN unexpectedly disconnects.

The first setting to check is auto-connect. Most VPN apps offer some form of automatic connection. Without it, your VPN may stay disconnected until you remember to open the app and turn it back on.

After a long flight, a trip through baggage claim and the rush to reach your hotel, that can be easy to forget. With auto-connect enabled, your VPN can attempt to restore its connection automatically when your device gets back online or joins a new network. Check your VPN app before traveling and make sure its automatic connection options are configured the way you want them.

THE TRICK TO SMOOTHER STREAMING AT HOME AND ON THE ROAD

The second setting to check is the kill switch. A VPN kill switch is designed to block internet traffic if your VPN unexpectedly disconnects. That helps prevent your device from simply falling back to an unprotected connection while the VPN is trying to reconnect.

However, kill switches do not all work exactly the same way. Some protect you only when the VPN connection unexpectedly drops. Others can be configured to block internet access whenever the VPN is not connected.

Android users may also have system-level options such as Always-on VPN and Block connections without VPN, depending on their device and VPN provider.

Some reputable VPN services also offer additional kill switch options on supported platforms. Keep in mind that stronger settings that block all traffic outside the VPN can interfere with local network features or internet access when the VPN is intentionally turned off. The important thing is to understand how your VPN's kill switch works before you depend on it while traveling.

There is one situation that can complicate things: the captive portal. That's the webpage airports, hotels and other public Wi-Fi networks sometimes require you to open before they grant internet access. You may need to accept terms, enter a room number or complete another login step.

Because your device does not yet have normal internet access, the VPN may not be able to connect until you finish that process. Strict kill switch settings can occasionally make this more difficult.

If you encounter a Wi-Fi login page, complete the network's sign-in process and then confirm that your VPN is connected before opening email, financial accounts or other sensitive services. Also make sure you are joining the correct Wi-Fi network. If you are uncertain, ask an airport employee, hotel staff member or business employee for the official network name.

Settings help, but reconnection speed also depends on the underlying technology your VPN uses. This is known as the VPN protocol. Different VPN protocols handle network changes in different ways. Some are particularly well suited to phones and laptops that frequently move between Wi-Fi and cellular connections. WHY YOUR VPN KEEPS GETTING BLOCKED AND THE SIMPLE FIX

Before your next trip, take a minute to check your VPN:

You should also test your setup before leaving home. Connect to your VPN, turn Wi-Fi off and switch to cellular data. Then turn Wi-Fi back on and watch what your VPN does. Does it reconnect automatically? Does the kill switch block traffic while the VPN is disconnected? How long does the connection take to return? A quick test can help you catch a setting that needs attention before you are relying on your VPN in an airport or hotel.

Most websites already use HTTPS encryption, so a brief VPN interruption does not leave all of your online activity exposed. Still, a VPN provides another valuable layer of privacy when you are using networks you do not control. The biggest issue for travelers is making sure the VPN actually reconnects when a phone or laptop moves between cellular service, airport Wi-Fi, hotel Wi-Fi and other networks. Turn on auto-connect, understand how your kill switch works and use a protocol that handles network changes efficiently. A few minutes spent checking your settings before a trip can help keep your VPN connection more consistent while you are on the move.

item.title: Navy veteran’s national anthem performance earns ‘best ever’ praise as he shares message of unity
item.description: Generald Wilson's national anthem performance before the Ole Miss-LSU rivalry game drew massive praise, with some fans considering it among the best ever.
item.content:encoded:
A retired Navy petty officer is earning national attention after his powerful rendition of the national anthem ahead of Saturday's highly anticipated Ole Miss-LSU matchup left some fans calling it the "best ever."

While Generald Wilson described the opportunity to perform at the game as a "blessing," to him, taking the field was about more than setting the stage for the rivalry.

"My point is always to create unity in the national anthem," Wilson told "Fox & Friends First."

THIS 'AMERICA THE BEAUTIFUL' RENDITION BEFORE THE FRANCE VS PARAGUAY MATCH WILL GIVE YOU GOOSEBUMPS

"We have our differences, we have our different opinions. That's just the way it is, [but] that doesn't mean that we shouldn't continue to love each other."

Wilson's message of unity has followed him throughout his "National Anthem Tour," which he said dates back to 1998 and has taken him before countless crowds at major sporting events across the country.

With time, the Navy veteran has become so recognizable to fans that he has noticed resounding enthusiasm before he even begins to sing.

"I'm starting to see the appreciation for patriotism, the appreciation for me singing," Wilson said. "It warms my heart. It makes me feel good. Before they even say my name, the crowd is going bananas, just to see me on the jumbotron."

OLE MISS, LANE KIFFIN SET FOR EMOTIONALLY CHARGED SHOWDOWN 10 MONTHS AFTER BITTER SPLIT

Wilson has also become a familiar voice for Ole Miss fans, returning to perform at a special game nearly every year since around 2012.

This year, Wilson returned for the Rebels' heated matchup against LSU, a team now led by former Ole Miss head coach Lane Kiffin.

"That crowd is awesome," Wilson said. "That's all I got to say about that."

Wilson also touched on his unlikely path to the national spotlight, recalling how his grandfather — whom the family called "Papa" — made a prediction about his future when he was just five years old.

"He told my uncles and my mom, like, 'You see that young man? He's gonna be somebody,'" Wilson recalled.

Expectations were not always high for those growing up in his hometown of Kinloch, Missouri, Wilson said, but he takes pride in the people who have gone on to pursue their calling.

"Most people say you wouldn't amount to too much coming out of there, but there are quite a few people that came out and are doing what God has called them to do," he said.

"So I'm just glad to be in that number."

item.title: Apple TV's 'The Savant' gets spring 2027 release date after postponing following Kirk assassination
item.description: Jessica Chastain's Apple TV series "The Savant" reportedly has a Spring 2027 release date after being postponed following Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.content:encoded:
Apple TV's "The Savant" has a release date after it was postponed in September 2025, shortly after Turning Point USA co-founder Charlie Kirk was killed while speaking at a college campus event that same month.

The show will be released in the spring of 2027, as reported by Deadline and Variety. A source confirmed the release timing to Fox News Digital. 

"The Savant" was set to premiere in September 2025 and followed an undercover investigator, played by Jessica Chastain, as she "infiltrates online hate groups in an effort to stop domestic extremists before they act," according to the show’s synopsis.

NETFLIX CLARIFIES CONTROVERSIAL 'NECK INJURY' POST ON CHARLIE KIRK'S ASSASSINATION ANNIVERSARY

"After careful consideration, we have made the decision to postpone ‘The Savant,’" an AppleTV statement from 2025 said at the time. "We appreciate your understanding and look forward to releasing the series at a future date."

At the time, Apple TV did not provide details of its decision. However, the show would have premiered two weeks after Kirk was shot and killed in what authorities described as an ideologically motivated attack.

Kirk’s alleged assassin was reported to have had a "leftist ideology" and harbored hatred against Kirk specifically.

Sensori.Ai founder Dr. A.K. Pradeep, a Silicon Valley entrepreneur, author and expert in neuroscience, consumer psychology, AI and marketing, spoke about what companies may consider in making the decision to delay a show release or a statement to Fox News Digital, comparing the thought process to that of politicians, who he said do the opposite of what corporations might do. 

Pradeep said successful politicians tend to trigger a fight-or-flight response within the limbic system of the voter.

"Corporations, unlike politicians, generally shy away from anything that triggers limbic responses. They never want to be caught in an Amygdala struggle, and try to position themselves as far from such struggles as possible."

"Apple’s decision is clear, and actually makes sense. Anything that can trigger a limbic system response is the last thing Apple would want to be associated with," he said. "Apple wants to be associated with Consumer Desire, and not Consumer Limbic responses. This is the real reason for the decision." 

HOW THE MEDIA, IN THE DIGITAL AGE, HELP FUEL A CLIMATE OF ANGER AND VIOLENCE

Chastain, an executive producer of "The Savant" as well as a star in it, spoke out against the decision to postpone in a Sept. 24, 2025, post to social media. She said she did not align with the decision.

"In the last five years since we’ve been making the show, we’ve seen an unfortunate amount of violence in the United States: the kidnapping attempt on Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer; the January 6th attack on the Capitol; the assassination attempts on President Trump; the political assassinations of Democratic representatives in Minnesota; the attack on Speaker Pelosi’s husband; the assassination of conservative commentator Charlie Kirk; the recent shooting at an ABC affiliate station in California; and over 300 school shootings across this country," she wrote on Instagram at the time. "These incidents, though far from encompassing the full range of violence witnessed in the United States, illustrate a broader mindset that crosses the political spectrum and must be confronted. I’ve never shied away from difficult subjects, and while I wish this show wasn’t so relevant, unfortunately it is."

Her post continued, "‘The Savant’ is about the heroes who work every day to stop violence before it happens, and honoring their courage feels more urgent than ever."

JESSICA CHASTAIN'S NEW HORROR MOVIE 'OTHER MOMMY' DROPS A TERRIFYING FIRST TRAILER FOR FANS

"While I respect Apple’s decision to pause the release for now, I remain hopeful the show will reach audiences soon. Until then, I’m wishing safety and strength for everyone, and I’ll let you know if and when ‘The Savant’ is released," she added at the time.

The actress and producer told Variety in April that the show would get a release date. On the show's page on AppleTV's website, the show's release date reads, "Coming soon."

item.title: Blue state gov ignites online firestorm with plan to send gov't into homes of newborn babies: 'Lunatic libs'
item.description: Massachusetts Democratic Gov. Maura Healey's Welcome Family program sparked a firestorm after a viral clip about home visits for new parents.
item.content:encoded:
Massachusetts Democratic Gov. Maura Healey set off an online firestorm over the weekend over a plan to expand the commonwealth's Welcome Family program, which she spoke about in a clip that went viral on social media.

Healey made the controversial comments in an appearance last week on Boston Public Radio, where she discussed the state’s taxpayer-funded plan to send nurses into the homes of new parents after childbirth.

"Everybody in the state, when you have a baby, you're going to have a home visit within days, weeks and that will be an opportunity for a healthcare provider to make an assessment to see if you need some additional support and resources," Healey explained.

The clip quickly made waves on social media, with conservatives blasting the governor’s government expansion.

GAVIN NEWSOM ACCUSED OF 'INFANTILIZING' PARENTS WITH DIAPER PROGRAM IN SCATHING WASHINGTON POST EDITORIAL

"Does this sound like a good idea?" conservative radio host Howie Carr wrote on X in a post viewed almost 2 million times.

"I’m sorry what?!" Conservative influencer account Libs of TikTok wrote on X in a post that was viewed over 2 million times. "MA Governor Maura Healey says everyone who has a baby will be visited in their home by a government appointed healthcare provider ‘to make an assessment’. Stay out of our homes you power hungry creep."

"IDK who needs to hear this… but the government DOES NOT OWN your baby," Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C. posted on X. "Everyone needs to re-read 1984. "

‘COVID 2.0’: LAWMAKERS PUSH BACK ON SWEEPING HEALTH 'POLICE POWER' IN KEY BATTLEGROUND STATE

"Lunatic libs," Sen. Tim Sheehy, R-Mont., posted on X.

Fox News Digital reached out to Healey’s office for comment.

Healey announced the expansion last week in a press release that described the program as "voluntary" and meant to "strengthen postpartum care and mental health support for mothers and families across Massachusetts, with a focus on reaching people earlier, making support easier to access and helping providers connect patients to care when they need it."

Postpartum care has been a major topic of conversation in Massachusetts in light of the highly publicized trial of Lindsay Clancy in the commonwealth, where a jury recently deadlocked and could not come to a consensus whether Clancy was guilty of killing her three young children. Clancy's defense team argued that she suffered from severe postpartum mental illness.

"Becoming a mother is a profound life change, and every parent deserves support—not just during pregnancy, but in the months that follow," Healey said in the release. "Postpartum depression, anxiety and other maternal mental health conditions are real medical conditions, and no mother should feel ashamed to ask for help or feel like she has to navigate this journey alone. We’re working to expand postpartum care, identify concerns earlier and connect families to the mental health support they need, because taking care of moms means taking care of the whole family."

Amy Carnevale, chair of the Massachusetts Republican Party, told Fox News Digital in an interview that "this is an example of the government overreaching."

"I'm a mom of three," Carnevale said. "I'm blessed to have three wonderful children. And, doctors, today, they ask about postpartum depression. They ask about the need for resources. So, there are plenty of resources available to women after they have children in Massachusetts and nationwide. And this example by Gov. Healey to send people into the homes of new moms is an example of government overreach and the Massachusetts Republican Party has been hearing from moms across the state, moms and dads across the state, really objecting to this new policy."

Fox News Digital’s Amanda Macias contributed to this report

item.title: Toronto Blue Jays and Baltimore Orioles face off in playoff-style game with wild card on the line
item.description: Trey Yesavage returns from the injured list to start for the Blue Jays against Shane Baz and the Orioles in a crucial Wild Card matchup tonight.
item.content:encoded:
We are entering the final week of the baseball season, and it is still a big week for a lot of teams. Many have already popped champagne bottles, knowing that they've made the postseason, but there are still quite a few that need to solidify their position.

Some of them are still looking to make the postseason, and others are just trying to lock down the division or Wild Card spot. Monday night we have two teams that are still in contention, but losses will knock them out quickly as the Blue Jays take on the Orioles.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Toronto Blue Jays have had a unique situation this season. They came into the season off a narrow loss to the Dodgers in the World Series. They lost Bo Bichette in the offseason, but added Dylan Cease. Many picked them to be a threat once again this season, but it never really came about. They started trading away players at the trade deadline, but instead of sinking further in the standings, they started winning games. It was kind of a down year overall, including for Vlad Guerrero Jr., who just hit his first homer at home a few games ago.

Tonight, the team turns to a playoff hero from just a year ago to try to keep their hopes alive.

Trey Yesavage toes the rubber tonight and brings a 5-5 record with a 3.65 ERA into the contest. He also carries a 1.14 WHIP and has 91 strikeouts over 93.2 innings of work. He is coming back from the injured list, so you do have to be curious about just how many pitches they will allow him today. He has faced the Orioles twice this season and allowed seven earned runs over 10.2 innings. The Blue Jays lost both games, and Yesavage gave up nine walks in those innings.

MLB WORLD SERIES FAVORITE FACES SERIOUS TROUBLE AS THE REGULAR SEASON ENTERS ITS FINAL FEW WEEKS OF THE YEAR

The Baltimore Orioles are still alive, but their hope is dwindling fast. If they lose these games, they will be knocked out quickly. The Blue Jays and Houston Astros are both three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card spot. The Orioles are currently sitting five games back. They were similar to the Blue Jays because they also had a really bad start, and then they traded away players. After the deadline, they started climbing back into the race. Now they have a sliver of hope, but it is likely too little, too late.

The Orioles are turning to Shane Baz to keep that little hope alive. For the season, Baz is just 6-15 with a 4.11 ERA and a 1.35 WHIP. The good news is that he at least has been healthy and eaten a ton of innings. He has a 3.92 home ERA for the season, slightly better than what he's done on the road this season. Baz is a bit hard to predict because he has multiple games with three or fewer earned runs, but then will sprinkle in a stinker of a game. He only faced the Blue Jays once this season and allowed one earned run on five hits over 5.2 innings.

Tonight is a game both teams need to win, and it should be treated essentially like a playoff game.

That doesn't mean there will be no offense, but I do feel like the managers will both have quick hooks. I still think we'll see some runs in this game, but given the importance of the game, big innings are unlikely. I think the Blue Jays win it, though. item.title: Trump's Greenland fixation revealed as wars expose why the Arctic island matters now more than ever
item.description: President Donald Trump's Greenland interest spotlights critical minerals and oil as Strait of Hormuz disruptions threaten global energy supplies.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's persistent interest in Greenland has put a spotlight on what lies beneath the vast Arctic island, including potentially valuable deposits of critical minerals and oil.

That focus intensified this week after Trump reached a security agreement with Denmark and Greenland that he is signing on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly on Tuesday — a deal the administration says is intended to strengthen U.S. influence in the Arctic and bolster long-term investment in the island.

The focus on obtaining control and influence in Greenland, which also has a highly strategic location in the world, comes as wars in Ukraine and Iran expose vulnerabilities in global energy supplies and the U.S. looks to reduce its dependence on foreign sources of critical minerals.

"One of the reasons that we are exploring for oil in Greenland is because of what's going on in the Strait of Hormuz right now," Robert Price, CEO of Greenland Energy Company and president of USFM Corporation, told Fox News Digital.

Price's two companies are pursuing separate oil and mineral projects in Greenland, including plans to drill an exploratory oil well in 2027 and ongoing mineral exploration in the island's west.

WHY TRUMP ZEROED IN ON GREENLAND, THE WORLD’S LARGEST ISLAND, MOSTLY COVERED IN ICE — IN 3 CHARTS

Those projects are taking on new significance as conflicts abroad strain global energy supplies and highlight vulnerabilities in critical supply chains. The Iran conflict has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical artery for global oil supplies, while the war in Ukraine has put energy infrastructure at the center of the conflict.

Trump announced an agreement with Denmark and Greenland on Friday that would expand the U.S. military presence on the island while keeping Greenland under Danish sovereignty. Full details have not yet been made public, but Fox News Digital obtained exclusive insights into some of the specifics of the agreement.

"We don't want to be dependent on China for our rare earth minerals, and we don't want to be dependent on Russia for them either," Price said.

"Critical minerals, they touch every part of our lives, which includes our cellphones, our computers, batteries, power storage, power generation," he said.

Price's USFM has been drilling around Disko Island in western Greenland for nickel, copper, palladium and cobalt, commodities used in electronics, batteries, energy and manufacturing.

"This mining district could be one of the largest mining districts in the world," he said, comparing its potential with Russia's mineral-rich Norilsk region.

The scale Price described has not been proven, with exploratory drilling still underway.

TRUMP'S AMBITIOUS ENERGY BET COULD BE A WINNING HAND AS THE WORLD BURNS MORE OIL, GAS THAN EVER

Greenland's potential riches aren't limited to minerals.

Price's Greenland Energy Company is pursuing permits for an exploratory oil well planned for 2027. Its licenses are on Greenland's eastern side, where Price said the geology resembles the petroleum-producing North Sea.

"Our licenses are similar to the same petroleum system as the North Sea," Price said, noting that his company has sampled oil on and below the surface.

But Greenland's value extends beyond what may lie beneath the surface.

Sitting between North America and Europe and extending into the Arctic, the island has played a role in U.S. defense for decades. The U.S. maintains Pituffik Space Base there, its northernmost Defense Department installation.

Price said Trump's emerging deal with Denmark and Greenland could provide greater security and give companies more confidence to invest in projects that take years to develop.

"What it does is it shores up long-term investment in Greenland, and that's what our projects are," Price said. "They're long-term investments from oil, gas, and minerals."

"We're really excited about this agreement," he added.

item.title: His home changed hands for $5. Could it happen to your family?
item.description: A South Carolina caregiver allegedly gained power of attorney over a 75-year-old with Parkinson's, then transferred his home via quitclaim deed for $5.
item.content:encoded:
A deed can change hands without a burglar breaking a window or a scammer hacking a computer. Sometimes the first warning signs are sitting inside county records, bank accounts and email inboxes, waiting for someone to notice.

A disturbing case out of South Carolina shows why families may want to put a few digital safeguards in place now. According to a local report, a daughter says her 75-year-old father, who had Parkinson's disease and a brain injury, became increasingly isolated after a caregiver entered his life.

Within weeks, the caregiver was named as his power of attorney. A quitclaim deed later transferred his Conway home to her for $5. His daughter also says bank statements show money moving from his account to the caregiver, including after his death. Conway police said they were investigating.

The allegations have not been proven in court. Still, the case raises a question every family with an aging or vulnerable loved one should consider: Would you know if someone changed a deed, moved money or took control of an important account? Technology cannot prevent every form of financial exploitation. However, the right alerts can create an early-warning system that makes major changes much harder to hide.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

MAN ACCUSED OF STEALING MORE THAN $735K AS POWER OF ATTORNEY TO PURCHASE PROPERTY, ONLYFANS AND LIFE COACHING

Home-title theft usually involves a criminal forging documents, impersonating an owner or recording a fraudulent deed. The allegations in this case raise a different concern. The daughter alleges that her father was vulnerable and may not have understood what he signed after the caregiver obtained power of attorney.

A forged deed can involve identity theft. When someone signs a document after alleged manipulation or coercion or when questions arise about whether that person understood what they were signing, the legal issues can involve undue influence, elder financial exploitation or abuse of legal authority.

Technology cannot determine what happened between two people. What it can do is flag events that deserve a closer look, including a new deed filing, an ownership change, a new lender, an unusual bank transfer or a change to an account's contact information.

The FBI has warned that quitclaim deed fraud can involve forged documents as well as relatives or close associates persuading older adults to transfer property for someone else's financial gain. The agency recommends monitoring property records and enrolling in county title alerts where available.

You do not need expensive technology to start watching for suspicious changes. Some of the strongest safeguards are free alerts already offered by county governments, banks and financial institutions. The key is setting them up before something happens and making sure the warnings reach someone who can act. Here are five digital safeguards worth putting in place.

DIY IDENTITY PROTECTION VS PAID SERVICES: WHAT WORKS IN 2026

Start with the government office that records deeds in the county where the property is located. Depending on the state, it may be called the county recorder, recorder of deeds, register of deeds or clerk's office. Many of these offices offer a free notification service. Look for names such as Property Fraud Alert, Recording Notification Service, Fraud Guard or Land Record Alert. Horry County, where the South Carolina property is located, now offers a free Recording Notification Service. It monitors the county's registry for new filings associated with a registered name and sends an alert when it finds one.

To find a service in your area:

Keep in mind that an alert does not stop a document from being recorded. Instead, it tells you something was filed so you can investigate quickly.

The reported deed transfer was only one warning sign in this case. The daughter also alleges that money moved from her father's bank account. Most banks and credit card issuers let you create alerts through their apps or websites. You will usually find them under Settings , Security , Alerts or Notifications .

Turn on alerts for withdrawals and outgoing transfers, new external accounts or payees, large purchases, checks clearing, low balances, password resets, new device logins and changes to contact information. Also consider setting transaction alerts at a relatively low dollar amount. Scammers sometimes begin with smaller transactions before trying to move more money.

Whenever possible, use more than one notification method, such as push notifications, text messages and email. Then review those settings every few months. A new phone, changed email address or bank app update can sometimes interrupt notifications.

A trusted contact gives a financial institution another person to reach if it sees signs of exploitation or cannot contact the account holder. That person does not automatically become a joint owner and does not receive power of attorney simply because they were named as a trusted contact.

For brokerage accounts, FINRA rules require firms to make a reasonable effort to obtain a trusted contact. The contact may be asked about the account holder's health, current contact information or possible financial exploitation. Being named a trusted contact does not give someone permission to trade, withdraw money or view account balances.

Some banks and credit unions offer similar protections voluntarily. Ask the fraud department or elder financial exploitation team whether it provides trusted contacts, read-only account access, extra confirmation for large transfers or additional review when money goes to a new recipient. Choose the person carefully.

If a daily caregiver already has access to finances, consider using a different relative, attorney or accountant as the trusted contact. That creates another set of eyes without handing over control of the account. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau says trusted contacts can help financial institutions respond to possible elder financial exploitation while allowing the account holder to retain control.

Alerts only help when they reach the right person. If someone else controls the account holder's phone or email, they may be able to delete warnings, change contact information or reset passwords before a family member notices. Start with the email account connected to banking, investment and property notifications.

Use a password manager to create and store a strong, unique password. Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). Review recovery phone numbers and email addresses. Check for unfamiliar forwarding rules and signed-in devices. Store backup codes somewhere secure that the person legally authorized to use the account can reach. Then protect the mobile carrier account too.

Add an account PIN and enable any protection the carrier offers against unauthorized number transfers. Someone who takes over a phone number may be able to intercept security codes and account alerts. Also, avoid sharing one online banking password among several relatives or caregivers. Instead, ask the financial institution about separate authorized access, a view-only login or another supported arrangement. Separate logins make it much easier to see who accessed or changed an account.

County and bank alerts provide a strong foundation, but they live in different places. A broader identity theft protection service can bring more warning signs together and provide help if identity theft becomes complicated.

Some services offer home title monitoring that looks for changes involving property ownership, new lenders, financing and notices of default. Depending on the provider and plan, you may also get alerts for suspicious activity involving checking, savings, credit, retirement and investment accounts.

In a situation like the South Carolina case, a recorded ownership change could potentially trigger an alert. Suspicious financial activity may also surface when affected accounts are connected and the activity meets the service's monitoring criteria.

Some identity theft protection plans also provide access to restoration specialists who can help if identity theft or home-title fraud occurs. However, monitoring has limits. Home title monitoring relies on county records, and newly recorded documents can sometimes take time to appear in monitoring systems. These services cannot block a deed, determine whether someone understood a document or prevent someone from misusing power of attorney.

Coverage, reimbursement and insurance benefits vary by provider and plan and may come with terms, conditions and exclusions. A dispute involving alleged coercion or a deed that someone actually signed may also be handled differently from a case involving forged identity theft.

Think of monitoring as an alarm, not a lock. It can warn you that something changed so you can investigate. It cannot make the change impossible.

See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com

A credit freeze remains one of the best tools for making it harder for criminals to open new credit accounts in someone's name. However, freezing your credit does not lock a property title. It also cannot stop activity inside an existing bank account or prevent someone from filing a deed. Use a credit freeze alongside property alerts, financial monitoring and secure account logins.

Digital alerts can flag transactions and account changes, but families should also pay attention to changes in behavior and access. Take a closer look if an older or vulnerable person suddenly stops communicating with family, becomes unusually isolated or has a new caregiver or acquaintance speaking for them.

Other warning signs include unexplained financial or legal decisions, missing bank statements or tax bills, unfamiliar people appearing on accounts, sudden password or address changes and property documents signed for little or no apparent value. One change may have a perfectly reasonable explanation. Several changes appearing around the same time deserve attention.

If something feels wrong, move quickly while preserving records that could help investigators understand what happened.

The CFPB says family members do not need every detail before reporting suspected elder financial abuse. Investigators can determine what happened.

THE SCAM TEXT TEST: SPOT DANGER BEFORE YOU TAP

The most unsettling part of this case goes beyond a home allegedly changing hands for $5. It is how many major changes may have happened before the family knew what was going on. No app can tell you whether a vulnerable loved one is being manipulated. A title-monitoring service also cannot replace regular conversations, careful legal planning and people you trust. Technology can still give families an important advantage: an earlier warning. Set up county property alerts. Turn on detailed financial notifications. Add a trusted contact. Secure the phone and email accounts receiving those alerts. Then consider broader monitoring if your family wants another layer of visibility across property, identity and financial accounts. The sooner you know something changed, the sooner you can start asking questions and take action.

item.title: AOC joins Macklemore frenzy in bizarre fundraising memo targeting pro-Trump billionaire
item.description: Rapper Macklemore gained a new ally in Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who blasted Robert Kraft for allegedly forcing Ed Sheeran to drop him from tour.
item.content:encoded:
Rapper Macklemore is getting a new ally as he continues to face backlash for his pro-Palestinian activism during his opening set for Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour earlier this month.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., invoked the ongoing controversy in a fundraising memo sent to supporters late last week, in which she also criticized billionaire Robert Kraft for reportedly getting Sheeran to drop Macklemore from his concert tour.

"Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez here. Billionaire stadium owner, Robert Kraft, did not like Macklemore, a Grammy-winning rapper, saying 'Free Palestine' on stage — so he made calls and the artist got pulled off of Ed Sheeran’s tour," the fundraising text obtained by Fox News Digital said.

"This is not just about a single musical act. This is about how a small handful of powerful people, like stadium owners, can threaten someone’s livelihood in order to prevent an entire massive issue from being spoken about — in this case, the genocide in Gaza."

COLIN KAEPERNICK ACCUSES NFL OF 'COLLUDING' AGAINST MACKLEMORE AMID 'FREE PALESTINE' CONTROVERSY

She went on to say Macklemore's plight represents a wider battle between social classes.

FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE

"Oligarchs and billionaires could just as easily prevent people from speaking out about AI, workers’ rights, or any issue they don’t like. That is what makes this a dangerous precedent. This moment is a test of how far the very powerful can go in censoring speech," Ocasio-Cortez said.

"And that’s why it’s important that we speak out about it. That we make clear that this is an abuse of power. And that we keep the focus on Robert Kraft and the way he’s using his influence to try to control what can and cannot be talked about in America."

MACKLEMORE DONATES $1M TO PALESTINIAN AID ORGANIZATIONS AFTER ED SHEERAN TOUR FALLOUT

The memo ended with the progressive congresswoman pledging to protect free speech and fight billionaires "who want to silence any form of dissent or peaceful protest," followed by the call, "Will you chip in $5 or any amount you can afford to power this movement for a better future?"

Macklemore, who was made famous for his song "Thrift Shop" in 2012, said "Free Palestine" during a Sept. 4 show in New Jersey while opening for Sheeran's tour. He then performed a song inspired by the Columbia University anti-Israel protests, according to Forbes, then declared, "The people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them. I say: Free Palestine. I say: Free Lebanon. Free Cuba to the Congo to Sudan to Iran."

ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO

Kraft, who owns the New England Patriots and their home turf Gillette Stadium, then threatened to cancel Sheeran's show there, Macklemore later wrote publicly. Kraft also warned that other stadium owners would follow suit.

And despite being told to stop, Macklemore said "Free Palestine" during the following night's show but clarified to Jews in the audience that his comments were aimed at Israel, not the religion as a whole.

ED SHEERAN FACES GROWING BACKLASH AS RADIO STATION BANS SONGS, PROTEST GROUPS RESPOND TO MACKLEMORE'S REMOVAL

It did not stop the backlash by pro-Israel groups and fellow musical artists, however, culminating in Macklemore being dropped from Sheeran's tour.

Kraft later told NBC News that his boycott was about a broader pattern of public discourse that he saw as harmful to the Jewish people. He told the outlet, "I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same — peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate."

The pro-Israel billionaire also pledged $2 million toward helping Palestinians amid the fallout.

Kraft also has close ties to Trump, despite a falling out over the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot. He donated money to Trump's first inauguration and was seen next to Trump in the Kennedy Center's presidential box earlier this year for a screening of the first lady's film, "Melania."

Kraft's wife, Dana Blumberg, is also a member of the Kennedy Center Board of Trustees.

Fox News Digital reached out to the New England Patriots' public affairs team seeking comment from Kraft.

item.title: Caleb Williams avoids major hamstring injury as MRI reveals a strain but no tear after Vikings game scare
item.description: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring strain versus the Minnesota Vikings, meaning he will return to team's lineup relatively soon.
item.content:encoded:
The most important MRI in the history of the Chicago Bears (maybe) returned good news on Monday because quarterback Caleb Williams avoided a major injury.

A source tells OutKick that Williams has a strained hamstring injury and that he is not expected to miss significant time following a major scare during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.

Williams has what is being described as a Grade 1 hamstring strain.

CALEB WILLIAMS CARTED OFF AT SOLDIER FIELD WITH APPARANT HAMSTRING INJURY

That means he may miss between one and three weeks while he rehabilitates. Bears coach Ben Johnson told ESPN1000 in Chicago on Monday he expects Williams to be "week-to-week."

Netflix Sports reported the Bears have not ruled out Williams for next Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

The source told OutKick that was a "very optimistic" outlook.

What is realistic is that Williams avoided a full detachment of his hamstring, which was the fear after he went down untouched during a scramble out of the pocket in the game against the Vikings.

SCARY SCENE AS JAYDEN REED CARTED OFF ON SPINE BOARD DURING PACKERS GAME AGAINST THE JETS

But the player's reaction was not indicative of the injury's seriousness, apparently.

Not even close, apparently.

His hamstring remains completely attached and structurally intact.

Williams was heard screaming as he lay on the turf and was eventually carted off the field amid the fear it could be his last time in uniform this season.

Williams, who has suffered and overcome hamstring issues in the past, is expected to begin a rehab program as early as Monday.

The Bears will go with backup quarterback Tyson Bagent in the games Williams misses, coach Ben Johnson said on Sunday.

item.content:encoded:
What is going on with the Los Angeles Chargers?

When the NFL schedule was released in the spring, it appeared the Chargers could start 2-0 with the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders on the docket in the first two weeks. Those prospective wins on paper turned into losses in reality.

The Chargers allowed 26 points and only scored 14 points in both losses. The defense, specifically, has allowed an average of 349 yards per game and has only one takeaway.

Pro Bowl safety Derwin James, who broke his left pinky finger, put the defense’s struggles bluntly when talking to reporters following the team’s loss Sunday to the Raiders.

"We got to look each other in the eye, man, and just tell the truth and just get better," he said, via the team’s website. "Because, right now, that s--- just looks trash. … I’m angry, but being angry don’t fix anything. Being angry don’t fix the problem that we have.

"We have to get it fixed. I feel like we’re a couple of plays away. It ain’t like we’re getting blown out. But we have to win these games, there’s no reason we’re going out there playing like that."

James has 17 tackles and a pass breakup in the first two games of the year but the rest of the team will have to come around to make a real impact going into Week 3.

"The Chargers are the second team in NFL history to lose back-to-back games by double digits with both coming at home against teams that had a sub-.200 win pct the previous season," OPTA Stats wrote on X. "The other was the 1926 Racine Tornadoes (Oct. 10-17), who played just one more game before folding."

The schedule doesn’t get any easier.
